basis: Mature T-cell lymphoma; extranodal involvement varies by site, with no additional organ established as affected in at least 30%.
Acute bacterial infection of the urinary bladder.
Sterol transport disorder; xanthomas lack demonstrated functional damage; atherosclerosis is separately coded; hematologic damage lacks clear >=30% evidence.
NF1 affects nerves and skin; bone cysts/scoliosis and structural heart anomalies each have supplied frequencies of 30-79%; Lisch nodules are non-damaging.
Suppurative infection in the intracranial or spinal subdural space.
IQSEC2-related intellectual disability and epilepsy; ocular findings are occasional or lack qualifying frequencies.
Complement C7 immunodeficiency; recurrent Neisserial infections are consequences, not intrinsic damage to another organ.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis encephalopathy; alacrima/ptosis and renal cysts/reflux reported in 1/1; skeletal anomalies omitted by cap; frequency estimates are fragile.
Nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration define Senior-Loken syndrome; intellectual disability occurs in 6/19 (~32%), just above threshold.
Congenital unilateral absence of the forearm bones and hand.
Corneal stromal deposits cause progressive visual impairment and recurrent erosions; disease is confined to the eye.
Myeloid marrow neoplasm with dysplasia, anemia and excess blood or marrow blasts.
Chronic immune-mediated eczema; asthma and allergic rhinitis are separate diseases; damaging ocular complications are not common enough.
Lower motor neuron degeneration; denervation causes skeletal muscle atrophy in nearly all patients. Respiratory weakness does not establish direct lung damage.
Hepatic steatosis with possible inflammation and fibrosis; associated diabetes, dyslipidemia and vascular disease are separate conditions.
Malignancy involving the oropharynx; the pharynx is explicitly assigned to the pulmonary axis.
Malignancy occupies the vestibulocochlear nerve; direct auditory nerve injury commonly causes persistent hearing loss (>30%).
Immune-mediated lichenoid inflammation destroys scalp hair follicles and causes permanent scarring alopecia.
Defining enterocolitis, immunodeficiency and encephalopathy; cerebral atrophy and bloody diarrhea occur in 3/3. Blood count changes do not establish intrinsic blood disease.
Endocrine pancreatic islet proliferation causes hyperinsulinemia/hypoglycemia or diabetes; ocular anomalies each occur in only 4/24.
Bagasse-associated hypersensitivity pneumonitis directly inflames pulmonary interstitium and can cause fibrosis.
Umbrella of inherited peptide metabolism disorders; no additional damaged organ is shared by most patients across the group.
Immunodeficiency and subcutaneous fat loss define disease; hypothyroidism 3/4; severe developmental delay 4/5. Ocular malformations 5/5 and cytopenias 4/5 omitted by cap.
Inherited keratinization disorder with ichthyosiform erythroderma and hyperkeratosis; no qualifying ocular damage is documented.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive spasticity; persistent GI dysfunction includes constipation 9/16 and reflux 8/16. Neonatal hypoglycemia is transient.
